summary: The module has the right skeleton (canonical isOpen/isOverdue/isDueIn7/isNew, a shared useNoticeSet hook, upsert sync with soft-delete, alert and litigation schemas, all RLS open to public with no auth.uid()-gated policies), but most of its automation does not run because code queries objects the migrations never created: both alert generators select gst_notices.hearing_date and clients.contact_person and the edge function inserts template keys that violate the email_outbox FK, the auto-close/due-date sweep filters a non-existent gst_case_folder_items.notice_id, and the notice drawer selects hearing_date, so no alert email, no auto-close and no per-notice drawer works (tsc already reports these; the build does not type-check). Dashboard numbers do not reconcile: tiles use the canonical functions, but every drill-down and sibling screen (All-notices list, Company Profile, GSTIN-wise, work queue, alert emails) re-implements them on different rows (original due_date only, any status, UTC-midnight arithmetic, un-deduped refunds/DRC-03, an unordered 1,000-row slice), and 'exposure' has three definitions. The sync write path still loses data at the edges (zero-row and failed-sub-fetch soft-deletes, merge-duplicates writing NULL over pdf_url/due_date, manual notices that cannot be inserted and would be soft-deleted by the next sync), and a client delete cascades through every litigation table while notice PDFs sit in a public bucket with anonymous update/delete. Litigation is CRUD only: no statutory clock is ever computed (matter_deadlines has no writer, litigation_rules is unused), payments mis-book pre-deposits, notices cannot be grouped into a matter, Phase 4 (unattended sync, retention) is not started, and the dashboard nevertheless states that an unattended sync runs at 06:00 IST.

findings.area: Alerts — queue-notice-alerts edge function and browser noticeAlertQueue
findings.screen: None (silence). Dashboard 'Send digest' and Reminders 'Run notice alerts' report 'No notice alerts due right now'
findings.issue: Neither implementation can produce an alert. The edge function selects gst_notices.hearing_date, which no migration creates and types.ts lacks, so PostgREST rejects the select, allNotices is null and the function returns {queued:0, message:'no notices'} with HTTP 200 on every cron run. Behind that: it selects clients.contact_person (column does not exist); it inserts email_outbox.template_key = 'notice_alert' / 'notice_alert_critical', which violates the FK to email_templates(key) because no such template rows are seeded; it looks for rule keys 'E4_hearing' / 'E5_limitation' while the seed uses 'E4_hearing_reminder' / 'E5_limitation_alert'; only a daily 04:00 UTC cron exists although the header promises a 15-minute run; and nothing writes captured/changed/removed notice_events (no trigger), so E1/E6/E9 have no source. The browser copy selects the same two missing columns, so runScheduledAlerts and processEventAlert also return 0 without an error.
findings.impact: Phase 1's promise (nobody has to open the app to learn that a notice arrived, is due or was missed) is not met, and because cron and buttons report success the team believes alerts are running.
findings.fix: Remove hearing_date/contact_person from the selects (hearings from matter_hearings, contact from clients.name/email); seed 'notice_alert' and 'notice_alert_critical' rows in email_templates or stop storing the shell key in template_key; align rule keys; add an AFTER INSERT/UPDATE trigger on gst_notices that writes captured/changed/removed events; schedule the 15-minute run; check every {error} and write a failure row instead of returning 'nothing due'; delete the browser duplicate so one implementation remains.

findings.screen: Notices Dashboard, work-queue footer link 'run the closing sweep'
findings.issue: runAutoClose and runDueDateSweep both query gst_case_folder_items.notice_id, a column that does not exist (folder items are keyed by client_id + case_id). Each pass returns an error before doing any work, so no notice has ever been auto-closed and no due date has ever been extracted; the toast shows 'Sweep errors: column ... does not exist'. The sweep is also manual-only, is silently capped at 1,000 candidates by PostgREST despite .limit(2000), and once fixed would send up to 1,000 UUIDs in a GET .in() list, beyond URL limits. The footer offers it as the remedy for stale rows and the SOP tells staff to click it after every sync.
findings.impact: LUT, refund and closure cases stay open forever, inflating Open and filling any deadline-sorted list with 2017-era rows (the reason the queue was switched to newest-first in #96); case rows never receive due dates, so DRC-01/ASMT-10 items never reach Overdue or Due-in-7.
findings.fix: Re-implement as a SQL function that joins gst_case_folder_items on (client_id, case_id); call it automatically after each client's notices pull and nightly via pg_cron; return counts and log a sweep-run row.

findings.screen: Notices Dashboard: click any work-queue row or Next-14-days chip
findings.issue: NoticeDrawer selects hearing_date from gst_notices. No migration creates it and types.ts does not have it (tsc: SelectQueryError 'column hearing_date does not exist' at NoticeDrawer.tsx:157). The query errors, data is null and the drawer renders 'Notice not found.' for every notice without showing the error. Verify with one anon-key select; if the column was added out-of-band, add the migration instead.
findings.impact: The per-notice view that every deep link targets cannot open, and 'Create Matter' (only reachable from the drawer) is unreachable.
findings.fix: Remove hearing_date from the select, or add the column by migration and fill it from folder JSON (sdtls.*.pershrng); render query errors instead of 'not found'.

findings.screen: Dashboard tiles 'Overdue & still open', 'Due in next 7 days', 'Exposure under dispute'; Next-14-days day click; category filter
findings.issue: Tiles use isOverdue/isDueIn7 (open only, no reply, extended_due_date ?? due_date, IST calendar date) but the list they open re-implements them: overdue = due_date < now for any status, any reply, ignoring extensions; due7 = original due_date, any status, computed as UTC-midnight minus Date.now() (a notice due today drops out after 05:30 IST); the Exposure tile opens every open notice rather than open notices with demand; a day click matches original due_date or issue_date and includes closed rows while the strip plotted extended dates of open rows; an active category filter is not passed to any tile link. The Overdue list therefore includes every closed historic notice with a past due date. The in-list 'Over Due Notices' / 'Due in 7 Days' presets use the same wrong logic.
findings.impact: Fails the roadmap's first acceptance check (tile counts equal their drill-down row counts); partners stop trusting the tiles.
findings.fix: Have AllClientsNoticesPage and the list presets import isOpen/isOverdue/isDueIn7/isNew and use the useNoticeSet rows; add filter=exposure (open and amount_of_demand > 0); match date= on effective due for open rows; carry category into tile links.

findings.screen: Every count and list (a client's rows vanish until the next good sync)
findings.issue: replaceNotices, replaceRefundApplications and replaceDrc03Filings always run the 'last_seen_at < pullTs => deleted_at' PATCH, including when the pull produced zero rows. A get/notices HTTP-200 error body is coerced to an empty list; a failed case/task/get call is swallowed to [], after which every case-task row of that client (DRC-01, ASMT-10, LUT, DRC-03 acknowledgements) is soft-deleted because it was not re-upserted; non-array refund/DRC-03 responses become [] and soft-delete every refund/DRC-03 row. The attempt is still logged as success with '0 entries'. Roadmap 0.1 required that a zero-row run never marks anything missing.
findings.impact: A transient portal problem silently removes a client's notices from tiles, lists and alerts; any future 'removed' alert would fire falsely.
findings.fix: Skip the soft-delete when rows.length is 0 or any sub-fetch failed; scope the PATCH to the sub-source actually read (separate source values for get/notices and case/task rows); treat non-array or error JSON as a failed pull and log it; block soft-deletes above a drop threshold (for example more than half of the client's rows).

findings.area: Sync write path — merge-duplicates writes NULLs
findings.screen: Drawer Documents tab; Overdue/Due-in-7 once the sweep works; refund sanctioned amount
findings.issue: The upsert payload sends portal-owned columns as explicit NULLs: case-task due_date:null, pdf_url:null whenever a PDF download fails, case_id:null on get/notices rows, refunds sanctioned_amount:null. PostgREST resolution=merge-duplicates updates every column present, so a transient download failure erases a previously captured PDF link, every due date the sweep writes for case rows is wiped on the next Sync All (the sweep only fills NULLs, so dates flap and need a manual re-sweep), and sanctioned_amount can never hold a value.
findings.impact: Derived data is not durable; once L-02 is fixed, case-row deadlines disappear after every sync.
findings.fix: Strip null-valued keys per row or send derived columns never; keep sweep output in a separate computed_due_date column (as the data model proposed) and define effective due as COALESCE(extended_due_date, due_date, computed_due_date); only write pdf_url after a successful upload.

findings.screen: Dashboard and All-clients list: 'Add Notice'
findings.issue: AddNoticeDialog inserts into gst_notices without portal_key, which the upsert migration made NOT NULL with no default, so the insert fails (tsc: 'portal_key is missing', AddNoticeDialog.tsx:73). Fixed naively, the row would still carry source='notices' and default last_seen_at, so the next Sync All for that client soft-deletes it because the portal did not return it.
findings.impact: Notices the portal does not list (summons, inspections, MOV, offline orders, appeals) cannot be tracked — the lifecycles the roadmap says need typed manual entry.
findings.fix: Insert with source='manual' and portal_key='manual:' + uuid; include 'manual' in useNoticeSet and AllClientsNoticesPage filters (the soft-delete PATCH already filters source='notices').

findings.screen: Notices Dashboard: 'Work queue — what needs action'
findings.issue: The queue does its own fetch: .limit(1000) with no ORDER BY and no source filter on a table already past 1,000 rows (arbitrary slice), then sorts by issue_date newest-first while the header pill says 'Open notices · earliest due first', and renders 50 rows. Its profiles query selects last_name, which does not exist, so the assignee list is empty and every owner shows '?' — bulk Assign cannot work. 'Hearings' is a regex on staff_status; 'Unassigned' ignores the free-text owner the edit dialog writes. The Team count does not equal the dashboard Open count.
findings.impact: The list meant to answer 'what must we do today' drops rows nondeterministically, buries overdue work under new arrivals and cannot assign owners.
findings.fix: Feed it from useNoticeSet; order overdue first, then effective due ascending, then priority, with undated rows in a 'Needs triage' tab; select profiles(user_id, first_name) restricted to staff via user_roles; derive the Hearings tab from matter_hearings.

findings.screen: Drawer 'Deadlines' tab (always empty); matter 'Limitation' field (always —); E5 limitation alerts
findings.issue: No code writes matter_deadlines (only readers exist); nothing computes litigation_matters.limitation_date, and computed_due_date is only a copy of notice.due_date set by the drawer; litigation_rules is seeded but fetchLitigationRules is never called. No appeal clock is created when an order date is logged, when an ORDRS/DRC-07 item is captured or when a refund is rejected; no pre-deposit is computed anywhere.
findings.impact: The highest-consequence date in GST litigation (the s.107 appeal limitation) lives only in staff memory; the roadmap's 3b check that a DRC-07 captured today shows an appeal last-date and pre-deposit fails.
findings.fix: A SQL function driven by litigation_rules that inserts matter_deadlines rows (appeal + condonation, rectification, RFD-08 reply, DRC-22 expiry) when order_date is set or an ORDRS/rejection item is captured; keep computed and override dates separate and show the basis.

findings.screen: Overdue / Due-in-7 tiles and Next-14-days once the sweep runs
findings.issue: extractDueDate reads raw.sdtls.duedate, raw.dtscn.duedate and raw.duedate. The folder page, built against live JSON, reads notices at sdtls.{dtscn|srscn|remnd|dtorder}.duedt and intimations at raw.duedt or sdtls.*.replyDuedt; only the RFD-08 (NOTAC sdtls.duedate) path matches. Dash-separated dates (used by refund items) are rejected. With several notice items in a case it keeps the EARLIEST date — the first notice's long-past deadline — so a case with a fresh notice reads as overdue, and the value is never refreshed once set. Personal-hearing dates (pershrng) are ignored. Positions doc section 4 records the wrong paths.
findings.impact: DRC-01/DRC-01A/ASMT-10 case rows get no due date (missed deadlines) or a stale one (false overdue).
findings.fix: Move subDetail()/replyFields() into a shared util and use them; take the due date of the latest notice or intimation not yet replied to; accept DD/MM/YYYY and DD-MM-YYYY; extract pershrng into a hearing row; recompute on every sync.

findings.screen: Open tile; Notice Summary Refund and DRC 03 rows
findings.issue: (a) notice_type matching /refund/ plus any ORDRS item closes the case, but refund ORDRS items include RFD-06 orders that may be rejections (sancordervo) and start an appeal clock — closing them hides it; (b) no rule for 'Voluntary Payment' (DRC-03 acknowledgement) rows, so about 146 such rows stay open and inflate Open (roadmap 0.4 named the 131 acknowledgements); (c) LUT closes only if an ORDRS item exists; (d) nothing closes a GSTR-3A notice once the return is filed although gst_filed_returns holds that fact, nor REG-20 drop, ASMT-12 acceptance or DRC-05 conclusion; (e) a DRC-07 should not close but move to 'Order received' with an appeal deadline; (f) rows without case_id (all get/notices rows) are never candidates.
findings.impact: Either stale open rows that staff must close by hand, or — once the sweep works — appealable rejections closed silently.
findings.fix: Read the order sub-type from raw_json and close only on sanction/payment/closure; on rejection or DRC-07 set stage 'Order received' and create the appeal deadline; add a Voluntary Payment rule (status Acknowledged); auto-close GSTR-3A by matching its return period to gst_filed_returns; record close_reason auto:* and an event for each.

findings.screen: Reports > GSTIN Wise Notice Count
findings.issue: The header comment asserts its grand total equals Notice Summary's, but it counts every gst_notices row (including the 'Refunds'/'Voluntary Payment' case rows computeNoticeSummary excludes) plus every refund and every DRC-03 row with no ARN dedupe, and keeps dedicated rows whose ARN is null, which Summary drops. Its Total/Open/Closed cells open /notices-all?client=..., which lists gst_notices only, so no client's count matches the list it opens. The Type filter drops refunds/DRC-03 here but not on Notice Summary.
findings.impact: Two report pages give different firm totals and per-client numbers do not match their drill-downs (roadmap 5.3 not met).
findings.fix: Group the useNoticeSet rows by client and call computeNoticeSummary per client; link Total to a merged per-client list or show refunds/DRC-03 as separate columns with their own links.

findings.screen: Dashboard 'Exposure under dispute' vs GSTIN-wise 'Exposure' vs Litigation MIS
findings.issue: Three definitions. The dashboard sums amount_of_demand (free-entered, and repeated across the ASMT-10, DRC-01A, DRC-01 and DRC-07 notices of one dispute) over open notices and labels the notice count 'matters'; GSTIN-wise and MIS sum matter demand heads over open matters; the tile opens all open notices. The tax/interest/penalty split and pre-deposit props of the tile are never passed.
findings.impact: The partner's key money figure differs by screen; the roadmap check 'exposure on the dashboard equals the sum over open matters' fails.
findings.fix: One SQL view: open matters' (tax+interest+penalty+cess − paid − pre-deposit) plus open unlinked notices with demand counted once per case; use it on all three screens with a matching drill-down.

findings.screen: Company List 'Delete Company' (and the Clients page)
findings.issue: Client delete is a hard DELETE and every module table cascades from clients: gst_notices, refunds, DRC-03, case-folder items, client_sync_log, notice_events (the audit trail), notice_alert_log, matter_deadlines, and litigation_matters with its stage history, events, documents, hearings and payments. Deleting a notice row also deletes its events. There is no archive flag, legal hold or deleted_at on litigation tables (roadmap 4.4).
findings.impact: One click on a sync-admin page irreversibly destroys litigation history the firm needs as evidence.
findings.fix: Archive instead of delete (clients.archived_at, filtered everywhere); ON DELETE RESTRICT on litigation FKs; ON DELETE SET NULL for event tables; legal_hold on matters; superadmin-only hard delete with typed confirmation.

findings.screen: Drawer and list PDF links
findings.issue: Notice, order, DRC-03 and manually uploaded PDFs go to the return-pdfs bucket, which was created public with policies 'Anyone can upload / view / delete / update'; a later migration's bucket insert is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so it stays public. Links are getPublicUrl URLs stored in pdf_url. (Roadmap 0.5 item still open.)
findings.impact: Show-cause notices and orders are readable by anyone with a URL, and anyone holding the bundled anon key can overwrite or delete the evidence.
findings.fix: Private bucket, no anon update/delete, short-lived signed URLs issued by an edge function; store storage paths rather than public URLs.

findings.screen: Team inboxes (once L-01 is fixed)
findings.issue: E3 has a 168-hour cooldown, so a notice gets one reminder near T-7 and none at T-3, T-1, T0 or while overdue; E3/E4 include notices already replied to; unassigned notices fall back to every staff member individually (N notices × M staff emails); the event-alert dedupe key omits the recipient, so only the first team member ever receives an event alert; E2 counts notices due today as overdue (instant comparison at 09:30) unlike the dashboard; E11 uses issue_date rather than first_seen_at and goes to partners in the edge function but to the whole team in the browser copy; quiet_hours, max_repeats and staff_notification_prefs are never read; the 'mode' body is ignored; email_outbox.dedupe_key has only a non-unique index, so the 23505 branch is dead and concurrent runs can double-send; notice_alert_log records 'sent' at enqueue time.
findings.impact: Alert fatigue for some, silence for others, and no escalation as a deadline approaches.
findings.fix: One server implementation; offsets 7/3/1/0 then daily while overdue capped by max_repeats; skip replied/closed; recipients owner, then team list, then partner; dedupe key per rule+notice+offset+date+recipient with a UNIQUE index and insert-on-conflict-do-nothing; honour quiet hours; log 'queued' and update on send.

findings.area: Sync & alerts card and header sync line
findings.screen: Notices Dashboard 'Sync & alerts' card, header 'N logins failed'
findings.issue: 'Emails sent today' is the literal '0'; 'Next scheduled unattended sync: 06:00 IST' is a literal although no scheduler exists; 'changed' counts rows whose pulled_at was refreshed, i.e. every row on every sync; 'Failed logins' reads only action='notices' logs while login failures are logged as action 'login_failed', and the Company List it links to uses the latest log of ANY action (including *_debug rows), so the header count and the filtered list disagree; 'with credentials' is simply clients not excluded from sync.
findings.impact: Staff are told data refreshes itself at 06:00 and that no logins failed when they did — the opposite of a health card.
findings.fix: Remove the static claims; count today's email_outbox sent/failed rows; add rows_new/rows_changed/rows_removed and run_id to client_sync_log and display them; derive failures from the latest login_failed or notices log per client and use the same predicate on Company List.

findings.screen: Work queue Owner/Unassigned; edit dialog 'Assign To'; drawer 'Assigned To'
findings.issue: Two owner fields that never reconcile. The workflow edit dialog writes free-text assign_to only and passes the old assign_to_user_id through, so no 'assigned' event; the work queue writes assign_to_user_id but logs no event, so E6 assignment emails cannot fire from either path; assign_to_user_id was added without a back-fill; dashboard 'Unassigned' and the queue ignore free-text owners while E11 treats them as assigned; clients.assigned_accountant, already used by Filing Status, is not used to default an owner for new notices.
findings.impact: No dependable answer to 'who owns this', so no ladder, no 'Mine' view and no accountability.
findings.fix: Back-fill assign_to_user_id by name match; use the staff picker everywhere; default the owner from clients.assigned_accountant on capture; emit 'assigned' events from a DB trigger so every writer is covered.

findings.screen: Notice drawer
findings.issue: Even when it loads, the drawer is read-only: no log reply/order/submission, no close-with-reason or reopen, no assign, no notes. Documents shows only pdf_url although the case folder's notices, replies and orders with attachments are already stored in gst_case_folder_items. There is no 'request documents from client' (E12) action, no reply template or precedent, no link to the client's 2B reconciliation / GSTR-3B workings for ASMT-10 or DRC-01C as the design proposes, and no /notices/:id route.
findings.impact: Preparing a reply still means hopping between the list, the folder page and the portal; nothing shortens time-to-reply.
findings.fix: Drawer v1 per roadmap 2.6: reply/order/close/reopen/assign actions, folder attachments via signed URLs, an E12 request with a per-category document checklist, quick links to the client's 2B/3B workings for the notice period.

findings.screen: n/a (root cause of L-01, L-03, L-07, L-08)
findings.issue: The commit gate is 'vite build' with strict:false, so nothing type-checks. tsc --noEmit already reports the runtime-breaking mismatches: missing portal_key (AddNoticeDialog.tsx:73), non-existent hearing_date (NoticeDrawer.tsx:157; noticeAlertQueue.ts:259 onward), profiles.last_name (NoticeWorkQueue.tsx:163), clients.contact_person (noticeAlertQueue.ts:259), AppUser.name (NoticeWorkflowListView.tsx:432,571). types.ts is hand-edited (close_reason inserted out of order) rather than regenerated, and the Deno edge function has no typing against the schema at all.
findings.impact: Column-name bugs ship green and fail silently at runtime.
findings.fix: Regenerate types.ts from project gcquafqxbykxkbexcdpy; add tsc --noEmit (at least for the notices/litigation files) to the gate; add a smoke script that runs each module select once with the anon key from .env.

findings.screen: Company Profile (/notices-company/:clientId) tiles
findings.issue: A third set of definitions: 'Over Due' and '7 Days Due' use original due_date only (no extension, no open or reply check, UTC-midnight minus Date.now()); 'Last 24 Hours' uses pulled_at, i.e. every row the last sync touched; Total adds refund and DRC-03 rows on top of their 'Refunds'/'Voluntary Payment' case rows. The query does not select extended_due_date or reply_date.
findings.impact: A client's profile disagrees with the dashboard and with the GSTIN-wise row for the same client.
findings.fix: Filter the useNoticeSet rows by client and use noticeDefinitions; 'New' from first_seen_at; ARN-dedupe refunds/DRC-03 as computeNoticeSummary does.

findings.screen: Notice summary by category; Notice Summary report
findings.issue: Only three description regexes (registration; return defaulter; ITC/liability mismatch) are applied; every other get/notices row is bucketed by the portal's raw type ('Notice', 'Order', ...). ASMT-10, DRC-01/01A, DRC-07, DRC-13, DRC-22, ADT-01/02, CMP-05, MOV-*, APL-02/04 arriving through get/notices never reach their canonical rows, which only case-task rows fill via CASE_NOTICE_TYPE_MAP; Appeal, Audit, Penalty, Ewaybill, AAR, TRAN 1 and Anti evasion are permanent zero placeholders. 'registration' lumps a REG-03 clarification with a REG-17 cancellation SCN and a REG-19 order. DRC-01B/01C detection relies on the literal text 'ITC mismatch|liability mismatch|DRC-01B|DRC-01C' — verify against live descriptions. litigationData LIFECYCLE_HINTS expect form codes that notice_type never contains.
findings.impact: Category bars mostly read 'Notice'/'Order', and category cannot drive priority, reply period or lifecycle.
findings.fix: Add gst_notices.form_code parsed from description, reference prefix or folder sdtls type, plus a mapping table (form_code to category, lifecycle, default reply days, critical flag) seeded from roadmap section 7.1; classify from form_code first.

findings.screen: Work queue priority chips
findings.issue: Priority is manual only. Nothing tags short-clock or coercive items (DRC-01B/01C 7 days, REG-17 7 working days, GSTR-3A 15 days, MOV-07, DRC-13/16/22) or notices carrying a demand as High, contrary to design section 7.2; the sync payload carries no priority.
findings.impact: Critical notices look identical to routine ones until someone triages them by hand.
findings.fix: BEFORE INSERT trigger: when priority is null and form_code is in the critical set or amount_of_demand > 0, set 'High'; never overwrite a staff value.

findings.screen: Category counts, Open/Overdue, case-folder page header
findings.issue: One portal case (ARN) yields one gst_notices row per task refId, all sharing case_id; each is counted separately in categories, Open and Overdue and each can become its own matter. When a task's refId equals a get/notices noticeOrderId the task row is skipped, leaving the get/notices row with case_id null — never linked to its folder and never a sweep candidate. The folder page header takes an arbitrary row (limit(1) without ORDER BY). Roadmap 0.1 'dedupe case-task rows by ARN' is not done.
findings.impact: One dispute can appear as several open notices; the same SCN can appear once as 'Notice' and once as 'DRC 01'.
findings.fix: One case row per (client_id, case_id) with task details in jsonb; when a task refId matches a get/notices row, copy t.arn into that row's case_id instead of dropping the link; order the folder-page lookup.

findings.screen: List inline Status, queue 'Change stage', drawer stepper, Due-in-7 breakdown
findings.issue: Four vocabularies: list inline and bulk status = Open | Closed; queue stages = Awaiting data, Reply drafted, Partner review, Filed, Hearing, Order, Appeal, Closed; the drawer maps by regex; the SOP tells staff to set 'Under Review' / 'Reply Drafted', which the list cannot set and shows as an empty select. Moving a notice to 'Filed' does not set reply_date, so it stays Overdue; 'Order' stays open with no appeal clock; closing never requires a reason; the tile's replies/appeals/hearings split is a regex on staff_status and is effectively always 0 for appeals and hearings.
findings.impact: A notice staff marked as replied keeps showing as overdue; stage-based views cannot be trusted.
findings.fix: One stage enum (the section 7.2 list) for list, queue and drawer; 'Filed/submitted' requires reply date or ARN; 'Closed' requires a reason; derive the breakdown from deadline types.

findings.screen: 'Due in next 7 days' tile, Next-14-days strip, E3 emails
findings.issue: isOverdue excludes notices with reply_date but isDueIn7 does not; the strip's reply_due chips and E3 reminders also ignore reply_date, so notices already replied to keep appearing as due this week and keep generating reminders.
findings.impact: The weekly plan is padded with finished work.
findings.fix: Add the reply_date check to isDueIn7 (or rename it 'awaiting reply') and reuse it in the strip and alerts; update positions section 2.

findings.screen: Work queue 'Days' column, drawer warning banner, alert 'days remaining'
findings.issue: daysRemaining/daysUntil compute Math.round((UTC midnight of the due date − now) / day). From 17:30 IST a notice due today shows -1 / 'Overdue by 1 day' and one due tomorrow shows 'Today', although isOverdue says neither. formatDate/fmtDate parse 'YYYY-MM-DD' as UTC and render in browser time (a day early west of UTC); the edge function's todayIST builds a shifted instant, so its day counts depend on run time.
findings.impact: Wrong urgency every evening; a met deadline shown as missed.
findings.fix: One util: today in IST as 'YYYY-MM-DD' and day difference via Date.UTC on both calendar dates; format dates from the string, not via Date.

findings.screen: Drawer Activity tab, notification bell
findings.issue: Bulk status and priority (list), bulk assign, priority and stage (queue) and matter demand edits write no events. The edit dialog initialises closeReason to '' and saves close_reason = null, so every save wipes an existing reason, including auto:* tags. actor_name is always null from the list (AppUser has no 'name'). Sync-side changes produce no events (no trigger), and notice_events rows are deleted with their notice (ON DELETE CASCADE).
findings.impact: Who closed what, when and why cannot be reconstructed for review or a client dispute.
findings.fix: Log from an AFTER UPDATE trigger on gst_notices (old/new diff, actor passed via RPC or a session setting); send close_reason only when edited and prefill it; use user.firstName.

findings.screen: Bell in the app header
findings.issue: The bell filters .neq('actor_id', userId) and .neq('actor_user_id', userId); PostgREST neq compiles to SQL <>, which is NULL for a NULL actor, so system events (auto-close, any future sync 'captured' event, matters created from the drawer without an actor) never appear. It is mounted twice (mobile and desktop) and only refreshes on mount or open.
findings.impact: The in-app channel hides exactly the automated events it should surface.
findings.fix: Use .or('actor_id.is.null,actor_id.neq.<id>'); mount once; poll or use realtime.

findings.screen: Drawer 'Create Matter'; Matters pages
findings.issue: Create Matter makes one matter per notice with lifecycle hard-coded 'demand', no demand heads, FY, section, officer or reference, no deadline and no actor, and swallows errors. There is no UI to add a notice to an existing matter or to review suggested groupings — linkNoticesToMatter, suggestMatters, updateMatter, closeMatter and addPayment are dead code (only createMatter is imported) — so an ASMT-10, DRC-01A, DRC-01, DRC-07 chain becomes four matters. Closing a matter leaves its notices open and vice versa.
findings.impact: The matter layer cannot represent a dispute's lifecycle, so MIS and per-matter exposure are unreliable.
findings.fix: 'Add to matter' picker (same client, same case_id or FY first) and a 'Suggested matters' review page built on suggestMatters; prefill lifecycle, demand and FY from the notice; on matter close offer to close linked notices with the same reason.

findings.screen: Matter detail Payments; Litigation MIS; client litigation PDF
findings.issue: The matter page adds every payment, including kind 'pre_deposit', to paid_total and never updates pre_deposit_total (the unused litigationData.addPayment splits them the other way), so MIS and PDF 'Pre-deposit' is always 0; totals are read-modify-write (lost updates under concurrency) with no edit or delete path; drc03_arn is free text, not validated against gst_drc03_filings although the sync now captures head-wise DRC-03 amounts; there is no pre-deposit calculator.
findings.impact: Outstanding demand and pre-deposit figures are wrong in MIS and client reports.
findings.fix: Derive paid and pre-deposit totals as sums over matter_payments in a view (or maintain them by trigger); pick the ARN from the client's gst_drc03_filings; compute pre-deposit from litigation_rules.

findings.area: litigation_rules seeds versus the CGST Act (verify against current law)
findings.screen: None yet (rules unused)
findings.issue: Seeds are partly right but incomplete for an engine: s.107 3 months + 1 month condonation and s.112 3 months + 3 months match the Act as generally applied; s.107(6) is seeded only as 10% of disputed tax — the full admitted-amount component and the monetary cap are missing (cap reported reduced from ₹25 crore to ₹20 crore each under CGST/SGST by the Finance (No.2) Act 2024 — verify against current law and effective date); s.112(8) is seeded at 10% (the post-2024 rate; previously 20%) with no cap — verify; 25% for s.129 penalty appeals matches; a pre-deposit for penalty-only orders introduced by a later Finance Act is not seeded — verify; the s.112 basis reads 'from APL-04' rather than communication of the order and the GSTAT transitional window for older orders is not modelled — verify current dates; REG-18/REG-24 '7 working days' are stored with unit 'days', so calendar arithmetic would under-state them; there are no keys for s.73(10)/s.74(10) order limitation, s.74A notice/order limits, s.75(5) adjournment cap or s.54(7) refund-order period.
findings.impact: Encoding these as-is would produce wrong pre-deposit amounts and short registration deadlines.
findings.fix: Add admitted-amount, cap and penalty-only keys with effective_from; a working-days unit with a holiday calendar; limitation keys for s.73/74/74A; partner sign-off on every value before the engine uses it.

findings.screen: Work queue 'Hearings' tab; Next-14-days; MIS upcoming hearings
findings.issue: Hearings live only in matter_hearings on the matter page. The queue's Hearings tab is a regex on staff_status; the dashboard never feeds 'hearing' or 'appeal_limitation' items to Next14DaysStrip although the strip supports them; E4 reads gst_notices.hearing_date (non-existent) instead of matter_hearings; litigation_matters.hearing_at is overwritten by whichever hearing was added last, even a past one, and MIS upcoming hearings reads that field; personal-hearing dates in folder JSON are not extracted; there is no Hearings page or ICS export.
findings.impact: A scheduled hearing can be missed while every dashboard view shows nothing.
findings.fix: Feed the strip and Hearings tab from matter_hearings (scheduled_at ≥ today); maintain hearing_at as the next future hearing by trigger; run E4 over matter_hearings; extract pershrng into hearings when a notice is linked.

findings.screen: Matters list vs Litigation MIS vs GSTIN-wise
findings.issue: Two matter-number generators: the matters page uses count(*)+1 across all years and clients, the drawer uses max(matter_no)+1; uniqueness is (client_id, matter_no), so cross-client duplicates are accepted (and a concurrent create produces them); the first matter of a new year continues last year's count. Status mixes 'open' (matters page) and 'Open'. The matters list decides open/closed by stage = 'Closed' while MIS, GSTIN-wise and the PDF use status, and the stage dialog offers 'Closed' without setting status, so a matter can be closed on one screen and open on the others.
findings.impact: Matter references quoted in letters can collide, and matter counts differ between screens.
findings.fix: DB sequence plus BEFORE INSERT trigger for matter_no with a global UNIQUE; CHECK on status values; remove 'Closed' from the stage dialog or sync status by trigger.

findings.screen: Notices Dashboard load and after actions
findings.issue: Each load runs at least nine independent queries with all aggregation in the browser: useNoticeSet pages the whole gst_notices table, the work queue fetches another 1,000 rows plus clients and profiles, client_sync_log is read without a limit (it grows by five or more rows per client per sync and is silently cut at 1,000), clients twice, notice_events twice, and the bell is mounted twice. Nothing refetches after Sweep, queue bulk actions or Add Notice, so tiles go stale. Alert generators do four to six sequential round-trips per notice and recipient.
findings.impact: Slow first paint as data grows (roadmap target under 1.5 s at 5,000 notices) and numbers that do not move after an action.
findings.fix: A notices_dashboard_summary() RPC returning tiles plus the top-N queue; react-query with invalidation on every mutation; retention and an (action, created_at) index on client_sync_log; batched inserts in the alert function.

findings.area: Row set behind the Open count
findings.screen: Overdue tile 'of N', Unassigned chip, 'need closing'; category click on Refund or DRC 03
findings.issue: Tiles count every gst_notices row, including DRC-03 acknowledgement ('Voluntary Payment'), LUT and 'Refunds' case rows that Notice Summary dedupes or excludes, so dashboard Open does not equal Notice Summary Open. Clicking the 'Refund' or 'DRC 03' category sets a filter classifyNoticeCategory can never return, zeroing every tile. 'need closing' is an ad-hoc heuristic (open, no due date, no status).
findings.impact: The headline open count overstates actionable work by the acknowledgement rows.
findings.fix: Define 'actionable' once (exclude acknowledgement categories or auto-close them per L-11) and use the same row set for tiles and Summary; map Refund/DRC 03 clicks to their case rows or disable them.

findings.screen: Notice Summary Refund/DRC 03 rows; Refunds and DRC-03 lists
findings.issue: isRefundClosed matches /disburs|withdraw|reject|recredit/ — no sanction or payment-order states and no hyphenated 'Re-credit'; verify against the live status list (the roadmap's live check found 22 refunds closed by RFD-06/PMT-03 still counted open). A DRC-03 'Pending for Action by Tax Officer' counts as open although it is a payment already made. computeNoticeSummary uses isRefundClosed while the drill-down pages use isRefundClosed || isClosed, and duplicate ARNs resolve first-wins in one and last-wins in the other. sanctioned_amount is never populated.
findings.impact: Refund/DRC-03 open counts overstate pending work and do not match their lists.
findings.fix: One shared status map per source (observed values to open/closed) with a fixture; capture RFD-06/RFD-05 amounts into sanctioned_amount.

findings.screen: All-clients list (spinner forever), dashboard digest, drawer
findings.issue: useNoticeSet ignores errors from the refunds/DRC-03 queries and does not paginate them; AllClientsNoticesPage.fetchAll has no try/catch, so a fetchAllRows error leaves the page spinning; runScheduledAlerts and processEventAlert treat a failed select as 'nothing due'; the drawer turns query errors into 'Notice not found'; Create Matter failures are silent.
findings.impact: Failures look like 'no data' — which is how the Critical defects above went unnoticed.
findings.fix: Check every {error}; show an error state with retry; paginate refunds/DRC-03 with fetchAllRows.

findings.screen: Company List status 'save failed'; 'New' tile
findings.issue: Rows without noticeOrderId/refId get 'hash:' (description|date) or 'case:'+arn keys. Two rows with the same key in one batch make PostgreSQL reject the whole upsert ('ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time'), so nothing is saved for that client; when the portal edits a description the hash changes, the old row with staff work is soft-deleted and a 'new' row appears with a fresh first_seen_at. Frequency should be verified on live data.
findings.impact: Whole-client sync failures and spurious 'New' notices that lose workflow data.
findings.fix: Dedupe the batch by portal_key before upserting; prefer stable identifiers (docId/applnId, task id) in keys.

findings.screen: Notices top nav tabs
findings.issue: Tabs point to the wrong destinations: 'Matters' opens /notices-all?filter=submitted (notices with a submission logged), 'Hearings' opens /litigation (the matters list), 'Work Queue' opens /notices-all (every notice including closed) and 'Clients' opens the GSTIN-wise count.
findings.impact: Partners cannot reach matters or hearings from the module's own navigation; 'Work Queue' opens an unfiltered archive.
findings.fix: Matters to /litigation; Hearings to a hearings list; Work Queue to open notices sorted by due date; Clients to /notices-company-list.

findings.screen: Litigation MIS
findings.issue: Ageing uses the matter's created_at (when it was keyed into the app), not the notice or order date; outcome is stored in closed_reason text, so win-rate and time-to-close are not reported; there are no officer, section or opened-versus-closed views and no Monday MIS email; exportClientLitigationReport exists but no screen calls it.
findings.impact: MIS understates the age of old disputes and cannot answer 'how are we doing'.
findings.fix: Age from the earliest linked notice or order date; add an outcome column with a CHECK; wire the client PDF into Company Profile and the matter page.

findings.screen: Outbox log on the Reminders page
findings.issue: send-gst-email has no attachment support (E1/E6 PDFs), never recovers rows left in 'sending' when an invocation dies, and sends one recipient per row; notice templates carry no deep link; portal text is interpolated into HTML unescaped; browser-queued alerts store the rule's template key, so the notice shell (pill and accent) is never applied.

findings.fix: Graph file attachments (or signed links), a reaper for stale 'sending' rows, a deep_link variable, HTML-escaping of variables.

metricDefinitions.note: Same closed-prefix regex everywhere (copied, not imported, in the queue and alert code), but different row sets: dashboard counts all gst_notices rows incl. Refunds/Voluntary Payment/LUT case rows; Notice Summary ARN-dedupes refunds/DRC-03; GSTIN-wise adds refunds/DRC-03 un-deduped; Company Profile excludes synthesized refund/DRC-03 rows; work queue sees an unordered 1,000-row slice.

Canonical = open, no reply_date, COALESCE(extended,due) < today IST. Drill-down list, in-list preset and Company Profile use original due_date only, any status, any reply, UTC-midnight minus now; alert digest counts due-today as overdue; queue/drawer day counts flip to overdue at 17:30 IST.
Canonical uses effective due and open status but not reply_date (unlike Overdue); drill-down/profile use original due_date, any status, and exclude notices due today after 05:30 IST.

Dashboard tile and its drill-down both use first_seen_at (consistent pair). Company Profile 'Last 24 Hours' and /notices-all?filter=last24h use pulled_at (every row re-pulled); the in-list 'Last 24 Hours' preset uses issue date. Tile label says 'since last sync' but the window is a rolling 24 h.

Dashboard: Σ amount_of_demand on open notices (duplicated across a dispute's notices), count labelled 'matters'. GSTIN-wise/MIS/PDF: Σ demand heads on open matters (status-based). The tile's drill-down shows all open notices.

Summary: notices minus Refunds/Voluntary Payment case rows plus ARN-deduped refund/DRC-03 keys. GSTIN-wise: all notices + all refunds + all DRC-03. Company Profile: notices + refund + DRC-03 synthesized rows. All-notices list: gst_notices rows only.
All use reply_date IS NOT NULL. Refund/DRC-03 rows carry no replied concept. Queue stage 'Filed' does not set reply_date, so 'replied' undercounts work staff marked as filed.

Notices: closed-prefix regex (consistent). Refunds: Summary uses isRefundClosed, the drill-down uses isRefundClosed || isClosed; duplicate ARNs resolve first-wins vs last-wins. Vocabulary misses sanction/payment-order states (verify).
Dashboard/queue: assign_to_user_id IS NULL (ignores free-text owner the edit dialog writes). Alerts: both fields null AND issue_date older than 48 h.

Dashboard: latest action='notices' log per client is 'failed' (login failures are logged as action 'login_failed' and are missed). Company List (its drill-down): latest log of any action, including *_debug rows.

Queue and tile breakdown: regex 'hearing' on staff_status. MIS: litigation_matters.hearing_at (last added hearing). E4: gst_notices.hearing_date, which does not exist. matter_hearings itself is not read by any summary.
Rounded instant arithmetic against UTC midnight; off by one from 17:30 IST compared with the string-date comparison in noticeDefinitions.
Matters list uses stage = 'Closed'; MIS, GSTIN-wise and PDF use status. The stage dialog can set stage 'Closed' without status, so screens disagree; status values mix 'open' and 'Open'.

All treat anything not 'Acknowledged' as open (drill-down additionally accepts the notice closed-prefix). Conceptually questionable: a DRC-03 is a payment already made, and Voluntary Payment case rows without a dedicated match count as open via null staff_status.
